## Appendix E — Q2 2026 Guidance (as stated April 28, 2026)

Management provided the following Q2 2026 outlook on the April 28, 2026 earnings call:

> Revenue in the range of $3.40 billion to $3.60 billion, representing approximately 18% year-on-year growth at the $3.45 billion midpoint. Non-GAAP gross margin of approximately 58%. Non-GAAP diluted EPS in the range of $3.40 to $3.80.

CFO Bill Betz characterized the guidance as reflecting continued automotive segment recovery, sequential Industrial & IoT stabilization, and the accelerating data-center ramp, while noting that the non-GAAP gross margin trajectory toward 58% confirmed the company's medium-term target range of 57–59% remained intact following the 2024–2025 inventory correction.

financials.key_finding: NXP Semiconductors is a $12+ billion revenue business that experienced its first meaningful revenue contraction in the post-Freescale era during fiscal 2025, when full-year revenue declined 2.7% to $12,269 million as automotive customers worked through channel inventory and communication infrastructure spending contracted sharply. Despite the top-line pressure, the company demonstrated structural profitability resilience: GAAP gross margin compressed only 170 basis points to 54.7% and GAAP operating margin fell to 24.8%, while non-GAAP gross margin held above 57% in the fourth quarter. The balance sheet reflects the legacy of two large leveraged transactions — the 2006 Philips spin-off and the 2015 Freescale acquisition — as long-term debt stood at approximately $10.97 billion at December 31, 2025, a 13% year-on-year increase driven partly by $1.87 billion of new debt issuance used to fund the $625 million TTTech Auto acquisition and refinancing of existing maturities. The debt load is manageable given EBITDA scale — implied gross leverage is approximately 2.2-2.4x NTM adjusted EBITDA — but it constrains capital allocation flexibility and has historically contributed to NXP trading at a discount to less-leveraged peers such as Texas Instruments and Analog Devices. The recovery trajectory entering 2026 is pronounced: Q1 2026 revenue of $3.18 billion rose 12% year-on-year and exceeded guidance, non-GAAP operating margin expanded 120 basis points year-on-year to 33.1%, and free cash flow reached $714 million (22% of revenue). Q2 2026 guidance of $3.45 billion at the midpoint implies 18% year-on-year growth, with management targeting non-GAAP gross margin of 58% — a recovery toward the 59-60% ceiling achieved at peak-cycle conditions in 2022. Full-year 2026 consensus EPS is approximately $13.89, implying forward P/E of approximately 25x at $340 per share. The data-center revenue ramp — guided to exceed $500 million in 2026 from $200 million in 2025 — introduces a high-multiple growth vector that, if sustained, could meaningfully compress NXP's cyclicality discount relative to peers.
structural_observations: Revenue base of $12.27B in FY2025 is diversified across four end-markets (Automotive ~58%, Industrial & IoT ~19%, Mobile ~13%, Communication Infrastructure ~11%), with automotive dominance creating both a durable competitive moat and meaningful exposure to global vehicle production cycles and OEM inventory management behavior.

Fiscal year runs January 1 to December 31; NXP reports quarterly with 13-week periods ending approximately the last Sunday of March, June, September, and December — Q1 2026 ended March 29, 2026. This calendar timing creates occasional comparability nuances of 1-2 days across quarters.

Non-GAAP gross margin progression: peaked at approximately 59-60% in 2022, compressed to ~57% in FY2025 (GAAP 54.7%) due to unfavorable product mix and lower average selling prices during the inventory digestion cycle; management guided non-GAAP gross margin to 58% in Q2 2026, indicating recovery on track with medium-term 57-59% non-GAAP target range.

Capital structure is levered: long-term debt of $10.97B at December 2025 (up 13.3% YoY, reflecting TTTech Auto funding and refinancing), against GAAP shareholders' equity of approximately $5.0-5.5B; debt-to-equity ratio of approximately 1.22x, which is approximately 20% above the semiconductor industry median; NXP targets gross leverage below 2x adjusted EBITDA over the medium term and executed a refinancing in April 2026 to extend maturities.

Capital allocation priorities in descending order: sustaining a growing quarterly dividend ($1.014 per share per quarter as of Q4 2025, implying ~$4.06 annualized or ~1.2% yield at $340/share), funding organic R&D (~$2B per year, approximately 16% of revenue), strategic M&A (TTTech Auto $625M in 2025), and share repurchases — NXP has reduced share count materially from ~340M shares at IPO to approximately 246M diluted shares as of Q1 2026.

Peer multiple comparison as of May 2026: NXP NTM EV/EBITDA of ~14.2x versus Texas Instruments ~18x, Analog Devices ~20x, Infineon Technologies ~12-13x, Renesas Electronics ~10-11x, STMicroelectronics ~9-10x, and Broadcom ~24x; NXP's discount to the analog/MCU group reflects its automotive concentration, leverage, and historical cyclicality rather than inferior franchise quality, and has narrowed as the 2025 inventory correction resolved.

Market capitalization of approximately $79-84 billion as of late May 2026 (reflecting the ~$293-341 share price range following Q1 2026 earnings; stock surged approximately 26% on the Q1 2026 beat); 52-week range of $183-$345 captures the full amplitude of the inventory-cycle trough and the subsequent recovery re-rating; one-year market cap appreciation of approximately 67%.

leadership.key_finding: NXP Semiconductors entered 2026 under a freshly installed chief executive — Rafael Sotomayor, 56, who assumed the CEO title on October 28, 2025, after a structured transition from predecessor Kurt Sievers. Sotomayor's ascent followed approximately eighteen months as President of the company and, before that, four years running the Secure Connected Edge division (industrial, mobile, and communications infrastructure), giving him direct P&L exposure to the segments where NXP is now generating the sharpest recovery growth. His academic credentials are engineering-heavy — Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering from Purdue, Master of Science in Electrical Engineering from Georgia Tech, MBA from Harvard Business School — and his pre-NXP career spanned senior roles at Intel, Motorola, and Broadcom, accumulating over 30 years of operational and business-development experience across the semiconductor value chain. CFO Bill Betz, an EVP who joined NXP from a prior semiconductor finance career, replaced the retiring Peter Kelly and has been the financial voice of the company since mid-tenure; Betz presented the April 2026 debt refinancing and framed the capital-allocation framework on the Q4 2025 and Q1 2026 earnings calls. The board of directors, ten members strong as of the June 2026 AGM, includes Rafael Sotomayor as the sole executive director; the remaining nine are independent supervisory directors with backgrounds spanning semiconductor technology, automotive OEM operations, private equity, and global financial management. NXP's corporate governance structure as a Dutch N.V. (naamloze vennootschap) concentrates formal supervisory authority in a one-tier board model with non-executive directors holding the majority. The PE sponsor era effectively ended post-IPO as KKR and its consortium partners have long since distributed their holdings, but the leverage philosophy embedded during the 2006 LBO — operating with substantial debt, aggressive share repurchases, and a lean central-cost structure — continues to define NXP's financial character under successive management teams.
research_notes_for_writer: Sotomayor transition timeline: confirm the exact dates of his President appointment (April 28, 2025) versus CEO appointment (October 28, 2025) and probe what the five-month overlap with Sievers signified — was it a genuine transition period or an unexpected delay? Pull the relevant 8-K filings for the formal board resolutions.

Bill Betz CFO appointment: research when Betz was named CFO (replaced Peter Kelly who retired), his prior background, and any public statements he has made about target leverage ratios, capital allocation priorities between buybacks and M&A, and margin expansion roadmap — the Q4 2025 and Q1 2026 earnings call transcripts are the primary source.

Board composition: the 2026 DEF 14A (SEC filing dated April 27, 2026) contains full biographies for all ten director nominees — extract names, tenures, committee assignments (Audit, Compensation, Nominating/ESG), and any automotive or technology operational backgrounds that provide strategic alignment with the SDV thesis.

Kurt Sievers legacy: research what Sievers accomplished as CEO (2020-2025) — CoreRide launch, Freescale integration completion, COVID supply-chain navigation, Qualcomm deal aftermath — and how Sotomayor has publicly framed continuity versus strategic pivots in his first six months of leadership.

Compensation structure: the DEF 14A will show CEO pay mix (base, target short-term incentive as % of base, long-term equity grant structure). Determine whether long-term incentive awards are PSUs tied to relative TSR or absolute revenue/EPS metrics, and how the program was restructured after 2025 revenue miss versus prior-year targets.

Private equity governance residue: confirm that KKR, Bain, Silver Lake, Apax, and AlpInvest no longer hold board seats or material voting stakes as of 2026 — verify via 13D/13G filings and the proxy's beneficial ownership table — and note what institutional shareholders (Vanguard, BlackRock, State Street) now constitute the dominant ownership base.

TTTech Auto management integration: confirm whether TTTech Auto's founding management (Georg Kopetz and team) retained leadership roles post-acquisition or departed, and what this implies for talent retention risk in the safety-critical software stack that NXP paid $625M to acquire.
